cards.explanation: The word is "spoken," friends. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) Job's words get the LORD's approval there, and the three friends' words don't.

The answer is that Job will pray for them, friends. The LORD says, "Then My servant Job will pray for you…" (Job 42:8) The friends are the ones who need the prayer, and Job is the one who gives it. The LORD says He will accept Job's prayer.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says Job will pray for them, "…for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly." (Job 42:8) The friends bring the offering, and the LORD says He will not deal with them according to their folly. I think that's a big relief for three men who just heard the word "wrath."

The word is "accepts," friends. The three friends go and do as the LORD told them, "and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer." (Job 42:9) That matches what the LORD said earlier: "…I will accept his prayer…" (Job 42:8) The friends obeyed, and the prayer was accepted.

The word is "restores," friends. "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) Notice what comes first: Job prayed for his friends. Then the verse says the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.

The answer is a piece of silver and a gold ring, friends. "And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring." (Job 42:11) His brothers, his sisters and everyone who knew him from before came to the meal. They consoled him and comforted him, and each one brought a gift.

The answer is True, friends! "So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first." (Job 42:12) Then the verse lists what Job owned: 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys. The latter days were blessed even more than the first.

The answer is a share of the inheritance, friends. "…their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers." (Job 42:15) Job had seven sons and three daughters. The daughters received an inheritance among their brothers, and that verse comes right after their names, Jemimah, Keziah and Keren-happuch.

The answer is to the fourth generation, friends. "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) That's children, grandchildren and on down the line. Job lived to see a whole family tree.
